newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia must drop "no-first-strike" - moscow official.
newsitem.headline: Russia must drop "no-first-strike" - moscow official.

text.p: Russia should abandon its principle of not using nuclear weapons first in response to an attack by another country with conventional weapons, a senior security official was quoted on Tuesday as saying.

"Naturally, we are not talking of a preventive nuclear strike, but if an aggressor starts a war against us using conventional weapons, we may respond with nuclear ones," secretary of the policy-making Security Council Ivan Rybkin told the Rossiiskaya Gazeta daily.
"Everyone must know that in case of a direct challenge our response will be fully-fledged, and we are to choose the use of means...including nuclear weapons," said Rybkin.

Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev had pledged that the Soviet Union would not use nuclear weapons first in any armed conflict. But Rybkin said that Russia, which inherited the bulk of the Soviet nuclear arsenals, should not follow this promise.

"We are reviewing political declarations of the past," Rybkin said. "Our people have spent decades buiding up a nuclear shield... And suddenly, without consulting anyone, someone says we are not going to use nuclear weapons first."
Rybkin said the present condition of Russia's armed forces was not as good as it was in the Soviet times and that this justified the change of principle of using nuclear weapons.
